title: Discord
intro: Bind a Discord bot to one of your saved agents. People talk to the agent in a direct message with the bot, or by mentioning it in a channel or thread. Each person, and each thread, gets a chat of its own.
name: Name
tokenHelp: From the Bot page of your application in the Discord developer portal (Reset Token). It is kept sealed and never shown again.
tokenSaved: Saved. Type a new token to replace it.
tokenSpace: The token has no spaces. Paste only the token, without the word Bot.
tokenShape: This is too short for a bot token.
anyoneWarning: This is for public channels and for agents that only read. Anyone who can reach the bot can talk to this agent: by direct message if they share a server with the bot, and in every channel where the bot can read and they mention it. People who are not on a list hold no permission of their own: the agent cannot save memory, propose triggers or take their files for them, and the sensitive actions stay closed. The agent's other tools still work for everyone. What people write in a public channel is untrusted text, and it can try to steer the agent (prompt injection). Give the agent read-only tools for this connection, and none that sends messages, spends money or changes files. Each person gets a chat of their own, and the number of messages a person can send in a minute is limited.
anyoneConfirm: I understand that anyone can use this agent, and that its tools should be read-only
allowIdsHint: A user ID or a channel ID (numbers)
rules: Listed people can write in a direct message and mention the bot in any channel. A listed channel lets everyone in it mention the bot there, but they get no permission of their own. In a server the bot answers only when it is mentioned or replied to, or inside a thread where it was mentioned. It never answers bots or webhooks, and its messages never ping anyone. Use channel IDs: a server (guild) ID matches nothing. IDs only, no names: in Discord turn on Developer Mode (Settings, Advanced), then right-click a person or channel and choose Copy ID.
badIds: These are not Discord IDs: {{list}}. Use the number from Copy ID (17 to 20 digits). Names are not accepted.
notifyHelp: Optional. A channel ID, or user: followed by your user ID to get them as direct messages.
noSenders: Nobody has written to this bot yet.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirmDelete.message: The bot stops answering, and the token saved with it is deleted. To set it up again you must enter the token again.

setup.title: How to make the Discord bot
setup.step1: At discord.com/developers/applications choose New Application and give it a name.
setup.step2: On the Bot page choose Reset Token, copy the token once, and paste it into the field Bot token here. Keep it secret.
setup.step3: On the same page, under Privileged Gateway Intents, turn on Message Content Intent. Without it the bot cannot read what people write in a server. Leave the other two intents off.
setup.step4: Optional: turn Public Bot off, so only you can add the bot to a server.
setup.step5: Type the Application ID (General Information) below, and open the link it builds. Choose the server, and keep the permissions as they are.
setup.step6: In the server, check that the role of the bot can see the channels it should answer in. Then list the channel IDs here, and mention the bot to try it.
setup.appIdHelp: The number from General Information of your application. It is not secret. It only builds the link; nothing is saved.
setup.appIdBad: The Application ID is a number of 17 to 20 digits.
setup.invite: Link that adds the bot to a server
setup.permissions: The link asks for these permissions (the number {{number}}):

perm.viewChannels: View Channels: to see where it is mentioned
perm.sendInThreads: Send Messages in Threads: to answer in threads
perm.attachFiles: Attach Files: to send files that the agent makes
perm.readHistory: Read Message History: to read a thread and the files of a message

setup.never: Never give the bot Administrator, Manage Messages or Mention Everyone. It needs none of them.

reply.off: The answer only (Discord has no typing indicator here)

answer.replyHelp: Progress and Live show one working message, and the answer replaces it. Edits are limited by Discord, so Live updates about once a second. A long answer goes on in new messages of at most 2000 characters.
answer.conversationHelp: Send !new in Discord to start a new chat. A message that starts with a slash may be taken by Discord for one of its own commands.
